property_summary: For any caller address X and any address A passed to setOwner, the reference contract only allows the initially-deployed admin to change owner (so owner can change via setOwner only when msg.sender == admin); the mutant removes that restriction and therefore for some fuzzed caller X the mutant allows owner to be set by non-admin callers while the reference does not.

For any caller of setOwner invoked by the contract's admin, the owner variable becomes exactly the address argument _owner passed in; the mutant instead sets owner = tx.origin so for some _owner (when tx.origin != _owner) the resulting owner differs, breaking the rule.

For all callers, only the original admin (the address that deployed C) can successfully call setOwner; the mutant that compares msg.sender to owner instead of admin allows a non-admin caller (when owner != admin) to call setOwner and thus changes owner for some inputs.

For every caller address x, only the original deployer (admin) can successfully invoke setOwner — i.e., after any call to setOwner by x, owner equals the value passed only if x == admin; the mutant mistakenly allows the current owner (which may differ from admin) to act as admin causing setOwner to succeed for non-admin callers when owner != admin.

For every caller address, only the original deployer (admin) can successfully change owner via setOwner; the mutant that checks msg.sender == owner instead of admin lets the current owner (if different from admin) change owner, violating this rule for some inputs.

For every caller address a and target owner newOwner, only the original deployer (admin) can successfully call setOwner(newOwner) — i.e., after any call to setOwner(newOwner) by any caller, c.owner() equals newOwner if and only if the caller was the admin; the mutant that checks msg.sender==owner instead of admin allows a non-admin (specifically the current owner when owner!=admin) to succeed and change owner for some inputs.

For any admin-invoked setOwner(_owner) call that completes, the reference implementation returns true; the mutant unconditionally returns false, so there exist inputs (an admin call) for which the return boolean differs.

For any caller who is the admin and any address _owner, calling setOwner(_) succeeds and the reference always returns true; the mutant may return false when passed the zero address (breaking the rule).
